papers.title: Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
papers.abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wi\'sniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.

papers.title: $G$-Equivariant Hilbert Schemes and Quadratic Forms
papers.abstract: For a finite abelian group $G$ acting linearly on the plane let $\mathcal{X}$ be the associated quotient stack. We analyze a fine moduli space which parameterizes zero dimensional substacks of $\mathcal{X}$ whose corresponding subschemes of the plane have a given representation type, denoted by $\mathcal{X}^{[\rho]}$. By means of a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem of To\"en we give explicit representation theoretic formulas of $\dim(\mathcal{X}^{[\rho]})$ for all $\rho \in \operatorname{Rep}(G)$ which are similar to the McKay correspondence. We also give a classification of all such quotient stacks according to an associated quadratic form called the Euler form. For $[\mathbb{A}^2/\mu_n]$ given by the cyclic action $\zeta \cdot (x,y) = (\zeta x, \zeta^{-1} y)$, we give an interpretation of the corresponding Euler form in terms of border strips which may be removed by a diagram, an equational characterization of $n$-core partitions, and the number of significant arrows of a monomial ideal as defined in "Smooth and Irreducible Multigraded Hilbert Schemes" by D. Maclagan and G. Smith.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Bundles on Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We study algebraic vector bundles on cluster varieties. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, every algebraic vector bundle is trivial on a cluster variety with principal coefficients at an acyclic seed of irreducible finite Dynkin type. The proof is based on integral contractions of cellular $\mathbb A^1$-chain complexes and successive freezing. We also construct smooth cluster varieties admitting indecomposable rank-two vector bundles, whose nontriviality is detected by quadratic Euler classes. The cellular calculation also gives a criterion for stable freeness and computes integral real cohomology and the images of cycle class maps.

papers.title: Normal bundles of hyperelliptic curves and uniform propagation of semistability
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus $g\ge2$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We prove that the normal bundle of the embedding of $C$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$, $n\ge3$, by the complete linear series of a general line bundle of degree $n+g$ is semistable if and only if $n\ge3g+1$. By openness, general complete embeddings of general curves of genus $g$ also have semistable normal bundle when $n\ge3g+1$. We then show that a general nonspecial curve of genus two and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ has semistable normal bundle except when $(n,d)$ is $(3,5)$, $(4,6)$, $(5,7)$ or $(6,8)$. The degenerations used in genus two extend to every genus $g\ge3$: semistability in all nonspecial degrees and dimensions follows from the cases $0\le d-n-g\le4g-4$. Together with a separate estimate for large $n$, this reduces semistability in each fixed genus to finitely many cases. The proofs combine degenerations to reducible nodal curves, explicit bounds on the degrees of subsheaves, and, in genus two, finitely many exact computations, which are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: A Comparison Theorem for $p$-adic GKZ Hypergeometric $\mathcal D$-Modules and Complexes
papers.abstract: We compare the $p$-adic GKZ hypergeometric complex with the hypergeometric arithmetic $\mathcal D$-module defined via six functors. Under the $p$-adic semi-nonresonance condition, the natural comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism. We prove concentration of the $p$-adic GKZ hypergeometric complex in degree $n$, establish overholonomicity under another non-Liouville hypothesis. When $(q-1)\gamma\in\mathbb Z^n$, we construct a Frobenius structure on its $n$-th cohomology and prove that its restriction to the nondegenerate locus is an overconvergent $F$-isocrystal of rank $n!\operatorname{vol}(\Delta)$.

papers.title: Covering plane curves over finite fields with lines
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $d\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of a geometrically irreducible reflexive plane curve of degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be covered by at most $\left(\frac{1}{d}+\varepsilon\right)q$ many $\mathbb{F}_q$-lines, provided that $q$ is sufficiently large. The same conclusion holds for $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible curves that are not geometrically irreducible, since they have only $O(d^2)$ $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. In particular, for sufficiently large $q$, the bound applies to every $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible plane curve of degree $d$ when $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)>d$. Our bound is asymptotically sharp. The proof combines Entin's Chebotarev density theorem for varieties over finite fields with the Pippenger--Spencer theorem on covers of nearly regular hypergraphs.

papers.title: Boundedness of polarized log Calabi-Yau fibrations
papers.abstract: We investigate the boundedness problem for log Calabi-Yau fibrations whose bases and general fibers are bounded. We improve the results in arXiv:2504.05243 from birational boundedness to actual boundedness, which confirms a conjecture of Birkar and Hacon when the boundary coefficients belong to a fixed finite rational set. We also get a new proof for the birational boundedness result in arXiv:2504.05243 which is substantially more conceptual.

papers.title: Classification of can-Var diagrams of mixed Hodge structures and monodromic mixed Hodge modules on $\mathbb{C}$
papers.abstract: By our previous work, the category of unipotent monodromic mixed Hodge modules on $\mathbb{C}$ is equivalent to the category of can-Var diagrams of mixed Hodge structures. In this paper, we show that the associated graded diagram with respect to the weight filtrations decomposes as a finite direct sum of four basic types tensored with pure Hodge structures, which we call a split graded model. We then show that every unipotent monodromic mixed Hodge module is represented by a split graded model together with a finite family of $\mathbb{C}$-linear maps. We also obtain an analogous description in the case where the monodromy has no eigenvalue $1$.

papers.title: Artin-Schreier curves of prescribed p-rank without extra automorphisms
papers.abstract: Let p be an odd prime. We study the Artin-Schreier analogue of Poonen's problem of constructing curves without extra automorphisms. An Artin-Schreier curve carries an unavoidable deck group Cp, so the smallest possible full geometric automorphism group inside the Artin-Schreier locus is Cp. We determine the exact numerical range in which this minimum is attained, for every p-rank. More precisely, for integers r >= 0 and N >= 1, there exists an Artin-Schreier curve X/Fp with g(X) = (p - 1)N/2, gamma(X) = r(p - 1), Aut_Fp(X) is isomorphic to Cp if and only if either r = 0, p does not divide N + 1, N >= 3 and (p,N) not equal to (3, 3), or r >= 1, N >= 2r and (r,N) not equal to (1, 2). All models are defined over the prime field by explicit equations together with elementary choices of auxiliary polynomials, and every excluded admissible case is shown to carry an extra geometric automorphism. The main structural input is the theorem of Valentini and Madan on the uniqueness of the rational subfield of index p outside three exceptional families. We exclude these families by intrinsic arguments: the genus and p-rank in most cases, Nakajima's bound on p-subgroups of automorphism groups of ordinary curves for the ordinary family, and the Lehr-Matignon normal form for isomorphisms of one-point covers for the monomial family.

papers.title: Geometry of some determinantal arrangements
papers.abstract: Let $D_{m,n}\subset\C^{m\times n}$ be the union of the zero loci of the maximal minors of a generic $m\times n$ matrix, and let $U_{m,n}$ be its complement. We show that $U_{m,n}\cong\GL_m(\C)\times\Gr(m,n)^\circ$, where $\Gr(m,n)^\circ$ is the open stratum of the Grassmannian on which all Pl\"ucker coordinates are nonzero. For $m\in\{2,n-2\}$ this gives closed formulas for the topology of $U_{m,n}$ and recovers results of Yim. Our main result, which is computer-assisted, is that $D_{3,5}$ is \emph{not} a free divisor. This answers a question of Yim. We determine $\Der(-\log D_{3,5})$ explicitly. It has projective dimension one, and it fails to be free exactly on the matrices of rank at most two. There the failure comes from a non-free transversal arrangement: the ten planes spanned by pairs of five general vectors in $\C^3$. Computations in further cases support the conjecture that $D_{m,n}$ is free only for $m\le 2$ or $n=m+1$.

papers.title: Gamma conjecture II and explicit Stokes data for a quadric projective bundle
papers.abstract: We study the connection problem for the quantum differential equation of the Fano fourfold $X=\PP_{Q^3}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$. The problem is to identify its canonical asymptotic solutions with exceptional objects and compute the associated Stokes data. We use exact Mellin--Bessel integral representations and uniform vector asymptotics on sectors wider than $\pi$, followed by analytic continuation that preserves the Gamma framing. Cohomological chiral symmetry and mutations of exceptional collections put all eight sections at a common phase. This proves Gamma conjecture II for $X$ and determines a full exceptional collection and its Stokes and central connection matrices at the unit Novikov point and a specified admissible phase. The chiral symmetry also gives a flat symmetric bilinear pairing, an orthogonality identity for the Stokes matrix, and an integral unipotent square root of the monodromy matrix for a full turn. We obtain explicit formulas for the connection data at the opposite phase; on the Gamma lattice, the half-turn acts by tensoring with a square root of the anticanonical bundle. The same spinor integral transform constructs two canonical Gamma sections for $\PP_{Q^{2m+1}}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$, $m\geq1$, at positive parameters with distinct spectrum. Their sectors have opening greater than $\pi$, and their leading constants are independent of the dimension.

papers.title: A complex associated to a family of ideals and applications to subspace arrangements
papers.abstract: We reprove and generalize a result of Derksen describing the Hilbert polynomial of the vanishing ideal of a transversal subspace arrangement in projective space. When the subspaces have all codimension 2, we describe explicitly the local cohomology modules of the corresponding defining ideal. This is achieved via a complex naturally associated to the subspace arrangement, whose basic properties are also investigated.

papers.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.

papers.title: Campana strong approximation on generalised Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

papers.title: On the Cohomology Classes of Certain Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
papers.abstract: We study the de Rham cohomology and Deligne splitting for a class of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms by introducing a modular weight grading. As an application, we compute a particular cohomology class that gives rise to generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
papers.abstract: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.

papers.title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Chai about the rigidity of Tate-linear subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$: we show that that a smooth subvariety of a central leaf of $\mathcal{A}_g$ which is Tate-linear at one point is Tate-linear at every point. This is achieved by a careful analysis of the $p$-adic monodromy groups of Tate-linear varieties, building on recent work of D'Addezio and van Hoften.

papers.title: Weighted, GIT and N\'eron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
papers.abstract: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the N\'eron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted N\'eron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the N\'eron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
papers.abstract: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.

papers.title: Open WDVV equations for non-commutative families of bounding cochains
papers.abstract: We derive the noncommutative open WDVV equations for the open Gromov-Witten superpotential introduced in joint work of the author and Solomon, extending the Solomon-Tukachinsky equations to noncommutative differential graded algebras. The resulting recursive formulas facilitate the computation of open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints for even-dimensional Lagrangians. We apply the open WDVV equations to compute all open Gromov-Witten invariants for the real loci of even-dimensional complex quadrics of dimension greater than two. These computations show that open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints can be nontrivial in arbitrary dimensions. We also construct a character for a natural subalgebra of big quantum cohomology associated to a Lagrangian endowed with a point-like bounding cochain. The character is in the spirit of the Kodaira-Spencer map of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono. Applying the character construction to the even-dimensional quadric illustrates how point-like bounding cochains refine the information about closed quantum cohomology obtained from weak bounding cochains of Floer theory. Open Gromov-Witten invariants with three boundary point constraints determine the two extensions of the character from the subalgebra to big quantum cohomology.

papers.title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $\kappa$-class dressing.

papers.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic \`a la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic \`a la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic \`a la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

papers.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

papers.title: Algebro-Geometric Invariants of Finitely Generated Groups (The Profile of a Representation Variety)
papers.abstract: If G is a finitely generated group, and A an algebraic group, then Hom(G,A) is a possibly reducible algebraic variety denoted by R_A(G). Here we define the profile function, P_d(R_A(G)), of the representation variety of G over A to be P_d(R_A(G))=(N_d(R_A(G)),...,N_0(R_A(G))), where N_i(R_A(G)) stands for the number of irreducible components of R_A(G) of dimension i, where 0\leq i\leq d, and d=Dim(R_A(G)). We then use this invariant in the study of fg groups and prove various results. In particular, we show that if G an orientable surface group of genus g\geq 1, then P_d(R_{SL(2,C)}(G))\neq P_d(R_{PSL(2,C)}(G)). We also show that the same holds for G a torus knot group with presentation <x,y;x^p=y^t> where both p,t are greater than 2, and that the same also holds when G is a the fundamental group of a compact non-orientable surface of genus g\geq 3. Further, we show that if a group G can be n+1 generated, and presented by <x_1,...,x_n,y ; W=y^p>, where W is a non-trivial word in F_n=<x_1,...,x_n>, and A=PSL(2, C), that then Dim(R_{A}(G)) is equal to Max{3n, Dim(R_{A}(G'))+2 \} \leq 3n+1, where G'=<x_1,...,x_n; W=1>. We also give a condition guaranteeing that the resulting algebraic variety is reducible.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil III: Geometric local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the third in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we make the reduction from global arithmetic intersection numbers for special cycles to the local geometric quantities in our companion papers. Building on our previous companion papers, we also propose a construction for arithmetic special cycle classes associated to possibly singular matrices of arbitrary co-rank.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil IV: Analytic local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the fourth in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we pin down precise normalizations for some $U(m,m)$ Siegel Eisenstein series, give local Siegel--Weil special value formulas with explicit constants, and record a geometric Siegel--Weil result for degrees of complex $0$-cycles. Using this, we complete the proof of our arithmetic Siegel--Weil results by patching together the local main theorems from our companion papers.

papers.title: Profinite rigidity of K\"ahler groups: Riemann surfaces and subdirect products
papers.abstract: This paper establishes strong profinite rigidity results for K\"ahler groups, showing that certain groups are determined within the class of residually finite K\"ahler groups by their profinite completion. Examples include products of surface groups and certain groups with exotic finiteness properties studied earlier by Dimca-Papadima-Suciu and Llosa Isenrich. Consequently, there are aspherical smooth projective varieties that are determined up to homeomorphism by their algebraic fundamental group. The main tool is the following: the holomorphic fibrations of a closed K\"ahler manifold over hyperbolic 2-orbifolds can be recovered from the profinite completion of its fundamental group. We also prove profinite invariance of the BNS invariant.

papers.title: Improved, sublinear projective Schwartz-Zippel and (sub)quadratic dimension growth bounds in arbitrary codimension
papers.abstract: We introduce a sublinear sharpened version of a classical projective variant of the Schwartz-Zippel bounds. Here, the sublinearity is in the degree, whereas the classical Schwartz-Zippel bounds are linear in the degree. We prove such sublinear bounds in several cases, including for unions of linear varieties. These bounds lead to a subquadratic dependence on the degree for projective dimension growth bounds in low dimensions. This improves on the quadratic dependence obtained by Binyamini, Cluckers and Kato in [BCK25] and thus brings the dimension growth upper bounds and lower bounds for the worst case closer together, a question asked by Cluckers and Glazer in [CG25]. We also address another question from [CG25], to treat the case of general codimension. To this end, we introduce a natural projection argument with pull-backs. We also give our main results for any global field instead of just $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Matrix Kloosterman sums and product-trace estimates for semisimple algebras
papers.abstract: Let $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, $E=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and $\mathrm{Tr}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E/k}$. For $r\ge 2$, $a\in k^{\times}$ and $x\in E^{\times}$, let $\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)$ be the number of $r$-tuples $(x_1,\cdots,x_r)$ in $(E^{\times})^r$ satisfying $x_1\cdots x_r=x$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(x_1+\cdots+x_r)=a$. We prove $\left|\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)-\left((q^n-1)^{r-1}+(-1)^r\right)/q\right|\le (r^n-1) q^{\frac{(r-1)n-1}{2}}$. This proves the square-root estimate predicted in Wan's conjecture and generalizes a previous result of Moisio and Wan. For a finite semisimple algebra $B=\prod\limits_{i=1}^s M_{d_i}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n_i}})$ over $k$ and a regular element $x\in B^{\times}$, the same method combined with Zelingher's formula leads to analogous square-root estimates.
